title: Popescu's local problem is resolvable at a regular prime with separable residue field
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $A$ a $k$-algebra of finite presentation, $\alpha:A\to\Lambda$ a homomorphism of $k$-algebras and $\mathfrak q\subset\Lambda$ a prime ideal, and let $\mathfrak h_A=\sqrt{H_{A/k}\Lambda}$ be as in [def-weil-pbc-popescu-resolution]. Assume (1) $\Lambda$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]; (2) $\mathfrak q$ is minimal over $\mathfrak h_A$ (a minimal element of the set of primes of $\Lambda$ containing $\mathfrak h_A$); (3) the localization $\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme]; (4) the residue field $\kappa(\mathfrak q)=\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$, a field extension of $k$ via $k\to\Lambda$, is separable over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension]. Then $k\to A\to\Lambda\supset\mathfrak q$ can be resolved [def-weil-pbc-popescu-resolution].

proof.text: If the regular local dimension is zero, apply the fully proved local resolution lemma and then the existing height-zero delocalization theorem with the given minimality.

Otherwise take d equal to the finite span rank of the maximal ideal. Regularity identifies its dimension with d. For I=H_{A/k}Λ, minimality of q over I.radical gives radical(IΛ_q)=qΛ_q by IsLocalization.AtPrime.radical_map_of_mem_minimalPrimes. Finite generation and Ideal.exists_pow_le_of_le_radical_of_fg give an exponent; increase it to n+1 to ensure positivity.
Apply the preparation lemma to obtain c, the polynomial evaluation, C, β and γ, parameter generation, ideal domination, controlled first/square annihilators and strictly standard powered parameters.

Prove the annihilator conditions for powers directly. Monomial-ideal membership implies that multiplication by any power of x_i is injective modulo powers of earlier variables: the earlier-variable exponent coordinates are unchanged. For the target quotient, induction shows Ann(r^(n+1))=Ann(r) from Ann(r)=Ann(r²), then applies it to c and 2c.
Apply the parameter quotient resolution lemma, then the existing eighth-power lifting theorem using the proved annihilator equivalences. This resolves γ over the polynomial base.
The polynomial base is smooth over k. Apply the fully proved smooth-base transfer lemma with β, γ, composition and ideal domination to finish.
